findings.md finding 4: the minted spec directory slug can run to 66+ characters (e.g. 'notify-window-graded-notification-urgency-beyond-quiet-hours-boolean'), eating a third of Windows MAX_PATH before the project directory itself is counted. hub/hub/spec_naming.py's MAX_SLUG_LENGTH (232) is derived from the 255-char storage contract (SPEC_PATH_MAX_LENGTH), not from any path-practicality bound - investigated a principled fix this iteration and am punting rather than shipping it: the one piece of information that WOULD make a bound principled - the real filesystem depth the slug lands at - is only knowable at mint time (api/v1/spec.py::_mint_document_path has `workspace: ProjectWorkspace`, whose `.root` is an absolute Path), but that path means different things in the two deployment modes CLAUDE.md documents: in native mode it is the real host path (Windows MAX_PATH genuinely applies), in Docker mode it is a container-visible path under AW_WORKSPACE_ROOT that has no fixed relationship to the host path length at all, and the Hub cannot always tell which mode produced the workspace it is holding. A bound derived from workspace.root would be correct sometimes and silently wrong (either too strict on Linux hosts, or not strict enough to save a Windows host) other times - exactly the per-machine tuning 'limits' forbids, just laundered through a variable instead of a literal. Two ways to actually close this, both are calls for you: (a) accept a conservative fixed cap (e.g. 60-80 chars) as a UX judgement independent of any platform's exact MAX_PATH, restoring something like the UI's old 64-char bound but now shared with the MCP path too, or (b) leave it be - the 255-char contract is real and enforced, this is a cosmetic long-path nuisance on Windows native installs only, not a correctness bug, and nothing has actually failed because of it yet.

dead_ends: Git Bash `date` on this machine prints UTC but labels it +0100, so it reads one hour EARLIER than real local time while claiming to be local. PowerShell Get-Date is correct. This matters more than it looks: a last_heartbeat stamped from Git Bash lands an hour in the FUTURE, the driver computes a negative age, concludes a live session holds the branch, and stands down until real time catches up. ALWAYS stamp last_heartbeat from PowerShell (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:sszzz') or from Python's datetime.now().astimezone().
git add on a path that was deleted and already unstaged aborts the whole add and stages nothing.
npx openspec status --change rejects names starting with a digit; npx openspec archive accepts them. Do not conclude archiving is blocked.
openspec archive prefixes the archive date, producing 2026-08-15-2026-08-13-... in a repo that already dates change names. Rename after archiving.

Keep .ps1 files ASCII-only. PS 5.1 reads BOM-less UTF-8 as ANSI and an em dash inside a quoted string breaks parsing several tokens away. Syntax-check with Parser::ParseFile, from the repo root - from hub/ the relative paths resolve to nothing and it reports a spurious FAIL.
PowerShell 5.1 Add-Content -Encoding utf8 writes a BOM. Use UTF8Encoding($false).
Editing a file with Python newline='\n' when git has it as CRLF shows as modified with an empty --numstat. git checkout -- it; it is whitespace-only.

Ending an autonomous-driver iteration with 'a background Monitor/Task will notify me when the builder/verifier run finishes' does not work: each Scheduled-Task firing is a brand-new process with no memory of anything a previous firing started, so the notification has nowhere to land and the whole turn is wasted. Three consecutive iterations (16:51, 17:06, 17:21 on 2026-08-15) each spawned a wait and ended immediately, while the run they were 'waiting' on had actually already finished at 16:09 - nobody checked the live Hub state instead of trusting the stale in-session assumption. If a run needs watching, poll synchronously within the same iteration (block on GET /tasks/{id} or /spec/evidence in a loop with sleeps, inside the one turn) until it completes or a firm timeout is hit, or better: before assuming a task is 'still pending', GET its current state from the Hub first - a prior iteration may have already finished the drive and just failed to log it.

The Hub is started as plain `uvicorn hub.main:app`, no `--reload`. It does NOT pick up code changes while running - a commit that changes hub/hub/ behaviour is invisible to the live server until it is killed and restarted (Win32_Process.Create, same command line, from hub/). Discovered 2026-08-15T16:00 after 6 commits' worth of hub/hub/ fixes (95f8fa4 through fcedde6) were verified only by pytest, not live, and the running Hub (up since 12:21) silently kept serving a40ac5b's pre-fix behaviour the whole time. Restart before any live-Hub verification of code changed since the last restart, every time - do not assume a Hub that answers /health is running current code.

The Scheduled Task fires every 15 minutes and never unregisters on a failed iteration - it only unregisters past stop_at or with no STATE.json.
